title: Patch: the card-picks upload and the dev fill and clear take the account's economy lock, so two writes at once can't lose one
thread:
**Issue #2045 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #2045: Patch: the card-picks upload and the dev fill and clear take the account's economy lock, so two writes at once can't lose one
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When two devices touch the same account's card cosmetics at the same time — say a phone uploads its saved picks while the desktop picks a new finish on that card — one device's choices can silently overwrite the other's. The same holds for the developer tools that fill or empty a test account's collection: a pack opened at the same moment can lose cards the opening just granted. After this patch all of those writes queue behind each other the way the rest of the economy's writes already do, so no change is silently lost.

## Why

`put_card_pick` takes `economy_lock_account` before its read-modify-write — its comment says why: "two devices' writes take turns, so neither's change is lost" (`crates/server/src/api/card_picks.rs:98-128`). But `upload_card_picks` (`card_picks.rs:206-215`), which merges a device's stored picks, takes no lock: an upload row committing between a PUT's `economy_card_picks_get` and its unconditional `economy_card_picks_put` is overwritten wholesale. The dev `fill` (`crates/server/src/api/dev.rs:192-211`) and `clear`/`clear_cards` (`dev.rs:280-291, 401-424`) likewise read quantities then write absolute upserts with no lock, while `give_xp` (`dev.rs:131`) and `fill_bar` (`dev.rs:318`) lock deliberately. The advisory lock exists and is re-entrant (`economy/store.rs:1467-1475`).

## Proposal

Call `tx.economy_lock_account(&profile.id)` at the top of `upload_card_picks`, dev `fill` and dev `clear`, inside their existing transactions. The in-memory fake serializes transaction bodies so the race is only observable on Postgres; a contract test can still assert the lock is taken (the store logs it) or record the reasoning in a comment, as `rewards.rs:291` does.

## Where it lands

`crates/server/src/api/card_picks.rs`, `crates/server/src/api/dev.rs`, `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `upload_card_picks` holds the account's economy lock across its read-merge-write
- [ ] dev `fill` and dev `clear` hold it across theirs
- [ ] No change to request or response shapes, or to what the fake answers
- [ ] Each lock site says why, as `put_card_pick`'s comment does

## Size and risks

Small: three one-line additions plus a contract assertion or comment. The only cost is a longer critical section on dev endpoints, which are low-traffic and dev-gated by design.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-8` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40509290399)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

**Goal.** `upload_card_picks` (`POST /api/card-picks/upload`), dev `fill` (`POST /api/dev/fill`) and dev `clear` (`POST /api/dev/clear/:part`, every part) each call `tx.economy_lock_account(&profile.id)` right after their transaction begins. That is before any read, and the lock is held across the whole read, merge and write. Each lock site gets a comment saying why, in the style of `put_card_pick`'s. Request shapes, response shapes and the fake's answers stay as they are. New API tests read the fake's call log and prove that the lock is the first economy or collection call of each route.

**Files to touch**

| Path | new/change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/src/api/card_picks.rs` | change | `upload_card_picks`: a lock call and its comment after `app.db.begin` |
| `crates/server/src/api/dev.rs` | change | `fill` and `clear`: a lock call and its comment after `app.db.begin` |
| `crates/server/tests/api/card_picks.rs` | change | two private helpers, `record_store_calls` and `economy_calls`; a new test `a_put_and_an_upload_each_take_the_accounts_economy_lock_before_they_read` |
| `crates/server/tests/api/dev.rs` | change | the same two private helpers; a new test `fill_and_every_clear_take_the_accounts_economy_lock_before_they_read` |

Do not touch:
- `crates/server/src/economy/store.rs`, `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs` or `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`: no store method changes.
- Any migration, `crates/server/README.md`, `spec/`, or any crate other than `jackioh-server`.
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/` or `bot/`.

Governing spec: §14.10 (the dev tools, R1300000), §14.2 with R1834000 and R1834001 (card picks), and R1301003 (the account's economy lock, already proven in `tests/store/contract.rs` by `r1301003_the_economy_lock_is_taken_per_transaction`). No new ruling.

**Steps**

1. `crates/server/src/api/card_picks.rs`, `upload_card_picks`. Insert the following between `let mut tx = app.db.begin(Some(&profile.id)).await?;` and `let owned = tx.economy_cosmetics_get(&profile.id).await?;`. It follows the style of the comment at `put_card_pick` (lines 99–101), which cites no ruling.
   ```rust
       // What the account owns is read and the rows it lacks are written: under the lock
       // `put_card_pick` takes, a `PUT` from another device takes its turn instead of writing over
       // an uploaded row, so neither's change is lost.
       tx.economy_lock_account(&profile.id).await?;
   ```
   Change nothing else in the file, the module doc comment included.

2. `crates/server/src/api/dev.rs`, `fill`. Insert the following between `let mut tx = app.db.begin(Some(&profile.id)).await?;` and the blank line before `let owned = owned_in(&mut tx, &profile.id).await?;`. It follows `give_xp`'s comment style (lines 128–131).
   ```rust
       // [[R1301003]]: the account's economy lock, as every pack opening takes: the quantities are
       // read and written back whole, so a pack opened at the same time takes its turn and no card
       // it grants is lost.
       tx.economy_lock_account(&profile.id).await?;
   ```

3. `crates/server/src/api/dev.rs`, `clear`. Insert the following between `let mut tx = app.db.begin(Some(&profile.id)).await?;` and `let mut written = 0;`. It goes once, before the `for holding in holdings` loop, and not inside `clear_cards` or any other `clear_*` helper.
   ```rust
       // [[R1301003]]: the account's economy lock, as every pack opening takes, held across every
       // part: each holding is read and offset to 0, so a pack opened or a game paid at the same
       // time takes its turn and none of its grants is wiped without its offsetting row.
       tx.economy_lock_account(&profile.id).await?;
   ```

4. `crates/server/tests/api/card_picks.rs`. Add these imports next to the existing ones: `use jackioh_server::db::fake::OnCall;` and `use crate::support::store::fake;`. Then add the two helpers below `refusal`. The first copies `record_store_calls` from `crates/server/tests/api/friends.rs` (lines 846–856).
   ```rust
   /// Every store method the fake is asked to run from here on, by name, in order
   /// (`tests/api/friends.rs`'s).
   async fn record_store_calls(app: &App) -> Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<String>>> {
       let calls = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
       let sink = Arc::clone(&calls);
       let hook: OnCall = Arc::new(move |method: &str| {
           sink.lock().expect("the call log").push(method.to_string());
           Ok(())
       });
       fake(app).lock().await.on_call = Some(hook);
       calls
   }

   /// The economy's and the collection's methods among `calls`, in order: what a handler reads and
   /// writes of the account's holdings (resolving the caller reads only `profiles.`).
   fn economy_calls(calls: &std::sync::Mutex<Vec<String>>) -> Vec<String> {
       calls
           .lock()
           .expect("the call log")
           .iter()
           .filter(|method| method.starts_with("economy.") || method.starts_with("collection."))
           .cloned()
           .collect()
   }
   ```
   Add the test at the end of the file (see **Tests**).

5. `crates/server/tests/api/dev.rs`. Add `use jackioh_server::db::fake::OnCall;` (`fake` is already imported). Paste the same two helpers word for word under the plumbing section, after `ok`. The file's header says each test file keeps private copies. Add the test after `r1300000_clearing_everything_empties_all_five_and_a_bogus_part_is_no_clear`.

**Tests**

- `crates/server/tests/api/card_picks.rs`, `#[tokio::test] async fn a_put_and_an_upload_each_take_the_accounts_economy_lock_before_they_read()`:
  1. `let app = test_app().await;`
  2. For the PUT: `let calls = record_store_calls(&app).await;`, then `let (status, body) = put(&app, TOKEN, json!({ "cardId": CARD, "foil": "foil-rainbow" })).await;`, then `fake(&app).lock().await.on_call = None;`.
  3. Assert `status == 200` (message `"{body}"`). Then, with `let asked = economy_calls(&calls);`, assert `asked.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("economy.lock")` (message `"{asked:?}"`) and `asked.iter().any(|m| m == "economy.cardPicks.put")`.
  4. Repeat for the upload, using `upload(&app, TOKEN, json!([{ "cardId": PLAIN_CARD, "border": "border-wood" }]))`. Assert 200, the lock first, and `economy.cardPicks.upload` in the log.
  - The PUT half passes today and guards the other side of the race. The upload half fails without step 1, because its first call would be `economy.cosmetics.get`.
- `crates/server/tests/api/dev.rs`, `#[tokio::test] async fn fill_and_every_clear_take_the_accounts_economy_lock_before_they_read()`:
  1. `let (app, dev, _other) = dev_app().await;`
  2. Loop over these paths, in this order: `"/api/dev/fill"`, `"/api/dev/clear/cards"`, `"/api/dev/clear/cosmetics"`, `"/api/dev/clear/jlore"`, `"/api/dev/clear/counters"`, `"/api/dev/clear/tracks"`, `"/api/dev/fill"`, `"/api/dev/clear/everything"`.
  3. For each path: record the calls, run `ok(&app, path, &dev, json!({})).await;`, set `on_call = None`, and assert that `economy_calls(&calls).first().map(String::as_str) == Some("economy.lock")` (message `"{path}: {asked:?}"`).
  - It fails without steps 2–3: the first call would be `collection.get` or an `economy.*` read.
- Commands:
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::card_picks::`
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::dev::`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo jackioh spec check`: the comments cite R1301003, which exists, and the new test names carry no `r<n>` token, so no `proven_in` changes.

**Done when**

- [ ] `upload_card_picks` locks the account before `economy_cosmetics_get` (step 1).
- [ ] `fill` locks before `owned_in`, and `clear` locks once before its loop (steps 2–3).
- [ ] Each of the three lock sites has its comment saying why.
- [ ] No request or response shape changed, and no file under `crates/server/src/db/` or `crates/server/src/economy/` changed.
- [ ] Both new tests pass, and so do the existing `api::card_picks::` and `api::dev::` tests.
- [ ] rustfmt, clippy, spec check and the cargo tests are green. The catalog and patches checks have nothing to claim: no card changes, so no fragment is needed.

**Risks**

- **Deadlock:** none new. Every other site (`put_card_pick`, `give_xp`, `fill_bar`, packs, rewards) takes the lock first in its transaction, before any row lock, and these three do the same. `pg_advisory_xact_lock` is re-entrant within a transaction, and none of the three nests a lock.
- **The fake:** its `lock_account` is only the `economy.lock` seam (`economy/store.rs:2152`), so the in-memory store answers exactly as before and existing tests stay green.
- **Flaky call log:** the hook sees every fake call app-wide. These tests start no match, and the log is filtered to `economy.` and `collection.`, so concurrent `profiles.` reads from auth cannot reorder it. Clear `on_call` after each request, as `friends.rs` does.
- **Determinism, replay and hidden information:** not touched. This is server-only, outside the pure crates.

**Open questions**

None needed for the build. Two decisions are recorded for review:
- **Where the proof goes:** API tests in `tests/api/`, not the `tests/store/contract.rs` assertion the issue suggests. No store method changes, the store's lock is already contract-tested, and only the handlers' call order can show this change.
- **Ruling citations:** the dev comments cite `[[R1301003]]` like `give_xp`'s, while the card-picks comment cites none, like `put_card_pick`'s. The rejected alternative was citing it in both files.
````
